samples.summary: PUT /content now rejects the exact maximum nesting the DOCX importer deliberately produces (CLI import 400s; GET→PUT identity broken)
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlock` counts a *cell block* per table entered: the top-level table is depth 0, the blocks in its cells depth 1 … so a chain of 32 tables has its innermost leaf paragraph at depth 32 and now trips `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` (docs-content.controller.ts:454). But `DocxImporter.convertTable` caps at `depth + 1 < MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` (packages/docs/src/import/docx-importer.ts:435), i.e. it imports tables at depths 0..31 — exactly 32 tables — and its own new test asserts `importedDepth(...) === MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` (packages/docs/test/import/docx-importer.test.ts). The CLI import path feeds that model straight to the endpoint: packages/cli/src/docs/docx-import.ts:74 → packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts `putDocContent`. So a .docx at the importer's own ceiling imports, then the whole PUT fails with a 400 instead of degrading. The same asymmetry applies to the frontend, whose `writeFullDocument`/`writeDocsRoot` accept that document (deepest *table* at depth 31 < 32), so a body the editor can legally hold can no longer be PUT back — the documented GET→edit→PUT identity (docs/design/rest-api.md) no longer holds at the ceiling. Either the controller should compare `depth > MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` (block-count semantics) or the importer should stop one level earlier.

samples.summary: New silent decline in YorkieDocStore.insertTableColumn/insertTableRow leaves Doc.insertColumn/insertRow half-applied — table attrs written without the matching cells/rows
samples.evidence: `YorkieDocStore.insertTableColumn` and `insertTableRow` now `return` without writing when the table sits past the readable nesting cap (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts, `isPastReadableNesting` gates). Their only caller does not know that: `Doc.insertColumn` calls `this.store.insertTableColumn(...)` and then unconditionally `this.store.updateTableAttrs(blockId, { cols: td.columnWidths })` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:1061-1062), so the table's `cols` attribute gains a column no cell node exists for — and `treeNodeToBlock`/`computeTableLayout` allocate a cell per (row, column), so the CRDT now permanently describes a wider table than it holds. `Doc.insertRow` has the same shape with `rowHeights` (document.ts:1008-1012). `Doc.mergeCells` (document.ts:1155,1184) loops `store.updateTableCell` per cell, so a per-cell decline leaves a merge half-written. The fix belongs either in the store (decline the attr write too / throw) or in these Doc mutators.

samples.summary: DocStore contract does not mention that writes may silently no-op, and MemDocStore never declines — the two implementations now disagree
samples.evidence: `updateBlock`, `updateTableCell`, `insertTableRow`, `insertTableColumn`, `setHeader` and `setFooter` on `YorkieDocStore` can now return without writing (warn only), while the interface they implement documents them as unconditional mutations (packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:23,46,47,94,98,102) and `MemDocStore` (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts) applies them always. Every `Doc` mutator and editor command in packages/docs is written against the in-package store, so behaviour that is exercised under MemDocStore in the docs suite cannot be reproduced under the collaborative store — the same 'written against the in-package store so it cannot pass there and fail under the collaborative one' parity rule the `batch()` contract spells out at store.ts:74-81.

samples.summary: New doc comment claims writeFullDocument is reached from replaceDocument, but replaceDocument is a cache-only no-op
samples.evidence: `warnDeclinedTruncatedRowsWrite`'s doc block (yorkie-doc-store.ts:515) and `writeFullDocument`'s (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3510-3522) say the refusal covers `setDocument`/`replaceDocument`. `YorkieDocStore.replaceDocument` only refreshes `cachedDoc` and never calls `writeFullDocument` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1177-1183), and `MemDocStore.replaceDocument` (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:77) carries no cap at all. The backend's `writeDocsRoot` comment repeats the same framing (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:361-368). A future reader will assume a guard that is not on that path.

samples.summary: Slides text-body block walk still uses MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH while the shared docs layout now truncates nested tables at 32
samples.evidence: The slides block validator still caps at `depth > MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:1191, constant at :817), so a deck may be accepted with table nesting one level past `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`. Slides text bodies are persisted and read back verbatim (no codec — see the comment at docs-content.controller.ts:381-388) but are laid out by the docs engine, whose `layoutCellBlocks` now renders anything at or past the cap as a single empty line (packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:145). The result is content a PUT accepts and the renderer silently drops; the two ceilings should be reconciled or the divergence noted.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. `assertValidBlock` (docs-content.controller.ts:439, guard at :454, recursion at :499-503) counts one depth level per table entered and applies `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` to EVERY block, so a leaf paragraph inside a 32-table chain sits at depth 32 and 400s; it is reached from PUT via assertValidDocsBody (controller:191 -> :316). The DocxImporter deliberately produces exactly that shape: nesting continues while `depth + 1 < MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` (docx-importer.ts:437, top-level depth 0 at :136/:264) and empty cells always get a paragraph (:444-451); its own test asserts the imported chain is exactly MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH tables (docx-importer.test.ts:1460). The CLI feeds that model straight to the endpoint (cli/src/docs/docx-import.ts:74 -> cli/src/docs/import.ts:181/:231 -> http-client.ts:496 putDocContent). The writer and reader disagree with the new controller check: writeDocsRoot refuses only when a *table block* is at depth >= 32 (backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:376 via hasDocsTableAtNestingCap :237), and treeNodeToBlock materializes a table at depth 31 with rows (crdt-tree.ts:225), so a document the writer accepts and a GET returns can no longer be PUT back — breaking the GET->PUT identity the same controller file relies on (:383-384, :421-422). No upstream guard trims depth before the PUT, so the site is reachable; this is a contract change breaking out-of-diff producers, squarely in the blast-radius lane at major severity.

finding.summary: New silent decline in YorkieDocStore.insertTableColumn/insertTableRow leaves Doc.insertColumn/insertRow half-applied — table attrs written without the matching cells/rows
finding.evidence: `YorkieDocStore.insertTableColumn` and `insertTableRow` now `return` without writing when the table sits past the readable nesting cap (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts, `isPastReadableNesting` gates). Their only caller does not know that: `Doc.insertColumn` calls `this.store.insertTableColumn(...)` and then unconditionally `this.store.updateTableAttrs(blockId, { cols: td.columnWidths })` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:1061-1062), so the table's `cols` attribute gains a column no cell node exists for — and `treeNodeToBlock`/`computeTableLayout` allocate a cell per (row, column), so the CRDT now permanently describes a wider table than it holds. `Doc.insertRow` has the same shape with `rowHeights` (document.ts:1008-1012). `Doc.mergeCells` (document.ts:1155,1184) loops `store.updateTableCell` per cell, so a per-cell decline leaves a merge half-written. The fix belongs either in the store (decline the attr write too / throw) or in these Doc mutators.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. `YorkieDocStore.insertTableRow` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3007-3012), `insertTableColumn` (3044-3049) and `updateTableCell` (3110-3121) silently `return` via `warnDeclinedTruncatedRowsWrite` when the table sits past the readable nesting cap (gate at 2956-2958). Their callers in packages/docs are unaware of the decline: `Doc.insertColumn` calls `store.insertTableColumn(...)` and then unconditionally `store.updateTableAttrs(blockId, { cols })` (document.ts:1061-1062); `Doc.insertRow` writes `updateTableAttrs(..., rowHeights)` before the row write (document.ts:1008-1012); `Doc.mergeCells` (document.ts:1153-1157) and `Doc.splitCell` (document.ts:1177-1185) loop `store.updateTableCell` per cell, so one declined cell leaves a merge/split half-committed while sibling spans land. No compensating guard exists on the write side: `updateTableAttrs` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3247-3274) has no nesting/truncation check and always calls `styleByPath`; `applyCellSpan`/`applyCellStyle` likewise. The only model-side cap guards found (document.ts:920-928, editor.ts:4232) cover `insertTable`, not row/column insert, merge, or split, and the editor entry points (editor.ts:4314-4323, 4341-4350) gate only on `blockParentMap` cell membership, which the outer table in the merge case satisfies. This is a changed store contract with unupdated callers leaving partially applied writes — in-lane for blast-radius and not refutable on any named ground.

finding.summary: `YorkieDocStore.updateBlock`/`updateTableCell` can now throw, but every out-of-diff caller reaches them through `Doc` mutators that never threw before (and `MemDocStore` still never throws), so the new refusal surfaces as an uncaught exception mid-command
finding.evidence: The new `assertReplacesNoTruncatedRows` gate in `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1829` (updateBlock) and :3020 (updateTableCell) throws a raw `Error`. Callers are unguarded: `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4185` (`this.doc.updateBlockDirect(cr.blockId, block)` on the cell-rectangle delete path) and the ~30 `Doc` mutators in `packages/docs/src/model/document.ts` that delegate to `store.updateBlock`/`store.updateTableCell`. None catches, and `MemDocStore` (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts) has no equivalent throw, so the `DocStore` contract in packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:23/102 now differs per implementation and code written against the in-package store passes there and throws under the collaborative one. Reachable only on a document that already holds rows past the cap, which is why confidence is low — but the throw escapes a keystroke/command handler when it happens.

verdict.reason: The finding's central claim — that a new `assertReplacesNoTruncatedRows` gate makes `YorkieDocStore.updateBlock`/`updateTableCell` throw a raw Error into unguarded callers — is not present in this repository. (1) The symbol `assertReplacesNoTruncatedRows` does not exist in any source file; the only repo-wide matches are in the review artifact `.agent-review/correctness/stage-detail.json`. (2) The cited locations are unrelated: yorkie-doc-store.ts:1829 is `const topLevelLen = region === 'body' ? 1 : 2;` inside `getCellSubPath`, and :3020 is a closing `withUpdate` call inside `insertTableRow`. (3) The real guards in the two named methods do NOT throw: `updateBlock` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1882-1889) and `updateTableCell` (:3112-3121) call `warnDeclinedTruncatedRowsWrite(...)` and `return` early; that helper (:532-538) is a bare `console.warn` with no throw. (4) The only `throw truncatedRowsError()` is at :3530 inside the private `writeFullDocument`, which neither `updateBlock` nor `updateTableCell` calls; its reachable callers are the treeless fallbacks in `setHeader` (:1035) and `setFooter` (:1089), while the incremental header/footer paths (:1046-1054, :1097-1103) also warn-and-return. The implementation comment at :511-531 states the design explicitly: incremental writers decline rather than throw precisely because `Doc` mutators and `MemDocStore` never handled a throwing store. With no throw on these paths, the asserted blast radius (uncaught exception escaping a keystroke/command handler via text-editor.ts and the `Doc` mutators) cannot occur.

finding.summary: The new `updateTableCell` / `updateBlock` truncated-rows refusal is gated on the *replacement* model, so every writer that replaces a cell/block with content that contains no table-at-cap walks straight past it and still deletes the peer rows the reader never read
finding.evidence:
The gate added in `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:3021` (`if (hasTableAtNestingCap(cell.blocks, rowDepth)) this.assertReplacesNoTruncatedRows(...)`) and its twin at `yorkie-doc-store.ts:1831` only consult the tree when the *new* model still carries a table at the cap. Out-of-diff callers replace cells/blocks with content that has none:
- `packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:1137,1155` — `Doc.mergeCells` resets every covered cell to a single empty paragraph and then `store.updateTableCell(blockId, r, c, ...)` for the whole rectangle. The covered cell's model has no table at the cap, so the guard is never asked, and the cell node in the CRDT — which may hold a table at `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` with rows this reader truncated — is replaced whole. The rows a peer wrote are deleted and replicated, which is exactly the outcome the new refusal exists to prevent. (The top-left cell, which *does* get a table-at-cap in its model, is checked against its own path, which holds nothing truncated, so it passes and then writes the table back rowless.)
- `packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:1183-1184` — `Doc.splitCell` does the same for restored covered cells.
- `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4177-4185` — the cell-range delete clears cells then `updateBlockDirect(cr.blockId, block)`; a user-intended delete, but it reaches `updateBlock` with the gate false as well, confirming the gate's shape rather than its intent is what decides.
The fix belongs on the new code: the tree check has to be driven by what is at the target path, not by what the caller is about to write (cheap pre-filter could be the old node, not the new model).

verdict.reason: The finding's core premise — that the truncated-rows refusal is gated on the *replacement* model — is not what the repository contains. `updateTableCell` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:3110-3121) derives `replaced` from the pre-write document (`resolveTableBlock(tablePath, docBeforeWrite).tableData?.rows[rowIndex]?.cells[colIndex]`) and tests `hasTableAtNestingCap(replaced.blocks, rowDepth)` before the tree probe `replacesTruncatedRows([...tablePath, rowIndex, colIndex], rowDepth)`. `updateBlock` does the same with `replaced = this.getBlockByRegion(currentDoc, blockPath, region)` (1881-1889), and `setHeader`/`setFooter` are keyed on the old `doc.header`/`doc.footer` (1046-1054, 1097-1103). The in-code comments at 3104-3109 and 1874-1880 explicitly state the keying is on the block/cell being replaced precisely because "the replacement need not carry the deep table at all for the write to delete it". The cited bypassing callers therefore do not bypass: `getDocument()` returns `cloneDocument(this.cachedDoc)` (926-928) and `Doc` holds its own clone (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:130,176), so `mergeCells`' `cell.blocks = [...]` (document.ts:1137) and `splitCell`'s reset (document.ts:1183) mutate only the Doc-side copy; the store's `docBeforeWrite` still carries the truncated table (treeNodeToBlock 596-633 yields `tableData.rows: []` at the cap, which hasTableAtNestingCap 454-465 still reports true), so the gate fires and the write is declined. The exact lines the finding quotes (3021, 1831) hold unrelated code. Refuted as not-present.

finding.summary: Dropping the merge-expansion budget from `normalizeCellRange`'s default makes `Selection.getNormalizedRange` unbounded for callers that neither paint nor write — including a per-keystroke arrow-key path
finding.evidence:
`normalizeCellRange`/`normalizeRange` now default `budgetCells = Infinity` and only `computeSelectionRects` (selection.ts:715) passes `MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS`. The new comments justify this by saying every remaining `getNormalizedRange` caller *acts* on the rectangle, but two out-of-diff callers do not:
- `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3378` — plain Left/Right/Up/Down with a selection collapses it via `getNormalizedRange`, using only `normalized.start`/`end`. This runs on every such keystroke and now pays the unbounded fixed-point expansion (superlinear in a peer-chosen row count) that the budget was introduced to bound.
- `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:501` — `formatSourcePosition()` (format painter, reached from `copyFormat()` at line 467) likewise only reads the ordered rectangle.
Neither writes anything, so the "a short rectangle corrupts a merge" rationale does not apply to them; they get the hang risk with none of the benefit. Fix belongs on the new code (pass a budget from these read-only callers, or keep the default budgeted and opt the writers out).

verdict.reason: The finding claims two out-of-diff read-only callers of `Selection.getNormalizedRange` pass no merge-expansion budget, leaving them unbounded. Both named call sites actually pass `MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS`. (a) The plain-arrow-key selection-collapse path is at packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3426-3435, and calls `this.selection.getNormalizedRange(layout, MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS)` with an explicit "Bounded: this reads start/end only … a plain arrow key runs it on every press" comment; the cited line 3378 is in an unrelated earlier branch with no `getNormalizedRange` call. (b) `formatSourcePosition()` is at text-editor.ts:543-552 and calls `getNormalizedRange(layout, MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS)`; cited line 501 is a comment in the format-painter section header. The constant is imported at text-editor.ts:11. Grep across the repo shows exactly five `getNormalizedRange` call sites in text-editor.ts (549, 3432, 4222, 4379, 4420); the three that use the `Infinity` default all iterate the rectangle's cells (4222 clears each cell, 4379 copies each cell, 4420 extracts block content), which is precisely the "callers that act on the rectangle" case the documented contract at selection.ts:908-919 reserves the exact default for. The evidence's assertion that only `computeSelectionRects` (selection.ts:722) passes a budget is therefore also false. Code is not present as described.
